name: firediff
description: Firestore security rules diff for pull requests: a CLI and GitHub Action that runs old and new rules in the Firestore emulator and shows who gained or lost access, with a replayable request for each change.

paragraphs: Diff Firestore security rules by behavior. firediff is a CLI and GitHub Action that runs the old and new versions of your firestore.rules side by side in the Firestore emulator. It sends both the same generated requests: signed-out users, strangers, owners, users with custom claims or role docs. Then it reports only the requests whose allow/deny flipped: who gained access, who lost it, and a request you can replay for each. It's deterministic, doesn't use an LLM, and never touches a real Firebase project.
This is the comment firediff posted on a pull request that changed allow read: if isOwner(uid) to allow read: if isSignedIn() and dropped the update rule's guard on role.
Try it in the browser → No install: paste two rules files and compare. The hosted playground takes small files (up to 150 generated requests, 5 s per comparison); for bigger ones, run it locally.
